newsitem.title: QATAR: Pakistani expats raise $1 bln for debt fund.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani expats raise $1 bln for debt fund.

text.p: Pakistanis living abroad have contributed more than $1 billion in response to Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's appeal last month to pay off the country's foreign debt, a Pakistani leader said on Saturday.

"Overseas Pakistanis have so far deposited more than $1 billion and more is coming daily," Ijaz ul-Haq, a member of Pakistan's national assembly said in an address to the Pakistani community in Qatar.
"The scheme has also generated a tremendous response within the country and the people have deposited more than one billion rupee with the banks," he said.
Ijaz ul-Haq, a former banker and son of the late president Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq, is heading a four-man delegation on a Gulf tour to seek Pakistani expatriate's support to the scheme.
The team has already visited Oman, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait.
"The country has run up more than $34 billion in foreign debt, of which $10 billion has to be repaid soon," Ijaz ul-Haq said.
Sharif launched his plan under the slogan "Qarz Utaro Mulk Sanwaro" (Pay off debt, set country right) tapping his countrymen's patriotism to help pay off more $30 billion in foreign debt.

Sadiq Hassan, general manager of Pakistan's United Bank Ltd branch in Doha, said he had collected 2.2 million riyals ($603,000) in the past three weeks towards the prime minister's debt payment scheme.
"More remittances are coming in daily and we hope to collect upto five million riyals ($1.37 million) by the end of April," he said.
